description:
`Kernel.send/2` is `@spec send(pid | integer, t) :: t when t: any` and
forwards its first argument to `extern "fz" defp fz_send(pid, t) :: t when
t: any` (lib/kernel.fz:27). A call `send(1, 42)`
(fixtures2/behavior/concurrency_ping_pong.fz) builds the row fz_send[int, int],
outside the extern's declared domain. The runtime accepts it (the fixture
passes today), so the declaration is narrower than the definition.

Today the raw declared return hides this. Once an extern's return is its
contract applied to its row, the row has no answer, the continuation becomes
unreachable, and the program traps.

Work: make the declaration truthful (verify in the runtime what fz_send
accepts), and scan every extern in lib/*.fz for a declared domain narrower
than its wrapper's @spec; each one found is fixed at the declaration in the
same commit, or reported if the runtime genuinely rejects the wider domain.
title: fz_send declares a narrower domain than Kernel.send forwards
